answer.root_cause: The nct6687d DKMS driver source calls strncpy() at nct6687.c:444 but never includes the header that declares it. After the system update, the newer clang/kernel build enforces C99+ rules where an implicit function declaration is a hard error (previously just a warning), so the module no longer compiles and the sensor driver fails to load.
answer.evidence: dkms build output: 'nct6687.c:444:2: error: call to undeclared library function 'strncpy' ... ISO C99 and later do not support implicit function declarations [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]  444 | strncpy(valcp, val, 16);  note: include the header <string.h> or explicitly provide a declaration for 'strncpy'  1 error generated.'  The file's include block (lines ~33-46) contains only <linux/acpi.h>, <linux/delay.h>, <linux/dmi.h>, <linux/err.h>, <linux/init.h>, <linux/io.h>, <linux/jiffies.h>, <linux/hwmon.h>, <linux/hwmon-sysfs.h>, <linux/module.h>, <linux/mutex.h>, <linux/platform_device.h>, <linux/slab.h> — there is no <linux/string.h> (or <string.h>), so strncpy is undeclared.
answer.fix: Add the missing header to the DKMS source: insert '#include <linux/string.h>' into the include block of /usr/src/nct6687d-1/nct6687.c (e.g. after '#include <linux/slab.h>'). Then rebuild and reinstall the module: 'dkms remove nct6687d/1 --all && dkms add nct6687d/1 && dkms install nct6687d/1' (or simply 'dkms install nct6687d/1' after editing), then 'modprobe nct6687' to load it and restore the fan/temperature sensors.
